Independent covariance integration, Hölder and uniform quantile gap bound; independent numerical beta evaluation
correctness.rationale: The posterior is its linear interpolant plus independent Gaussian bridges in the positive gaps. On [a,b] of length ℓ, let U=B_a and D=B_b−B_a. Their covariance is −aℓ and Var(D)=ℓ(1−ℓ), so the interpolant covariance at offsets u,v is a(1−a)−a(u+v)+(1/ℓ−1)uv. Wick's rule gives conditional-mean risk 2∬C²+4∬C(K−C); triangle integration gives ℓ⁴/90 and a(1−b)ℓ³/12+(1−ℓ)ℓ⁴/45, respectively for the two unweighted integrals. This yields the frozen formula, with zero-length gaps contributing zero. The uniform grid gives (5m²−5m+2)/(90m⁴) for m=n+1. Near-minimizers have maximum gap tending to zero since the remainder is at least ℓ⁴/45 per gap and the grid gives O(m⁻²) total risk. Discrete Hölder yields the cube of the converging Riemann sum of [a(1−b)]^{1/3}ℓ as a lower bound for 3m²R. For attainment, put g(t)=[t(1−t)]^{1/3} and I=∫g. On every equal-g-mass gap, a(1−b)ℓ³≤(∫gap g)³=(I/m)³. On the middle half of any gap, t(1−t)≥ℓ/8, so equal mass also forces maximum gap O(m⁻³⁄⁴), and ∑ℓ⁴≤(max ℓ)³=o(m⁻²). This establishes the same limsup directly, including the endpoints. Independent evaluation gives 0.0496233141903951098 and a 10.6780344572888 percent improvement over 1/18.
residual_risks: The result concerns noiseless deterministic nonadaptive point readings of the pinned standard bridge. 1/18 is the scaled uniform-grid limit, not its finite risk.
No finite-budget quantile optimality, uniqueness, or adaptive/noisy result is inferred. The recorded numerical examples alone do not prove the asymptotic theorem.

originality.rationale: Credit the previous exact two-reading case, established smooth-functional quadrature and the classical cube-root design mechanism. The supported distinction is the elementary all-design gap identity and a sharp optimum over arbitrary deterministic bridge point designs with the full nonlinear conditional mean, including endpoint control. A matching curve of the local density in another information class is not by itself a lower bound for the richer conditional-mean problem.
residual_risks: Classical linear quadrature and nonlinear optimal-design literature may contain a more general reduction; Benhenni–Cambanis full text was unavailable. The similar density rule is not claimed as a new general design principle.
Bounded source comparisons do not establish historical priority; the fixed-two-reading overlap is substantial but not equivalent to the asymptotic claim.

Resultary 5b6200720fdd fixed-budget baseline; Santin's distinct equal-spacing objective
value.rationale: For a canonical nonlinear Gaussian path functional, the theorem gives an exact risk evaluable on any mesh, proves an optimum for the leading risk over all deterministic designs and provides simple attaining nodes. The nonuniform design gives a quantified 10.68 percent gain relative to the natural equally spaced benchmark. That is a useful design result even though the underlying cube-root mechanism is familiar and it does not optimize each fixed budget.
residual_risks: Practical gain is for this idealized risk and observation model; it is not a claim of robustness under noise or model misspecification.
